paper.title_en: Investigation of the impact of the nuclear surface-width parameter b on α-decay half-lives within the proximity potential model
paper.abstract_en: We investigate ground-state-to-ground-state (<math altimg="si154.svg"><mrow><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>→</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></math>) α decay in heavy even–even nuclei (84 ≤ Z ≤ 92) within the Prox-77 proximity-potential framework combined with the WKB approximation. Particular emphasis is placed on the nuclear surface-width parameter b, which influences the geometry of the interaction barrier and hence affects the WKB penetrability and the resulting half-lives. The parameter b is determined from the combined proton–neutron density using Myers’ geometric prescription based on the surface slope <math altimg="si155.svg"><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi>ρ</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow></math>. To examine the effect of neutron-density profiles on the total matter density and the extracted surface-width parameter, two limiting configurations are considered: neutron skin-type (NST) and neutron halo-type (NHT), where NHT refers to a phenomenological diffuse neutron surface, not a genuine few-body halo. The calculated half-lives reproduce the overall experimental systematics, with the NHT configuration yielding a lower RMSD of <math altimg="si156.svg"><mrow><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>10</mn></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></mrow><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo linebreak="badbreak">/</mo><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>exp</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> (decreasing from 0.513 to 0.368 in Region I, NpNn < 0, and from 0.336 to 0.301 in Region II, NpNn > 0). For a common subset of nuclei for which finite and bounded effective preformation factors (<math altimg="si8.svg"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mi>f</mi><mi>f</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>) are obtained in both configurations, the average difference between the two model predictions is <math altimg="si157.svg"><mrow><mo>〈</mo><mo>|</mo><mstyle mathvariant="normal"><mi>Δ</mi></mstyle><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>10</mn></msub><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>|</mo><mo>〉</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0.161</mn></mrow></math> in Region I and 0.150 in Region II. The extracted effective preformation factors are inherently model-dependent and exhibit configuration-dependent trends as a function of the normalized valence-nucleon product, reflecting the sensitivity of the inferred systematics to the adopted neutron-density profile and the associated barrier geometry. Overall, the present analysis demonstrates that α-decay observables are sensitive to the neutron-density profile through the surface-width parameter b, highlighting the role of density-informed surface properties in proximity-based descriptions of α decay in heavy nuclei.
